name: Mbedam
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Foba K'ayyang, Mai 2021. Phonologie, morphologie et syntaxe du mbudum [xmd], Univ. de Yaounde, 484pp; also Ndokobai 2011 Esquisse phonologique/orthographique (SIL Cameroon, site Cloudflare-blocked).

sources.citation: Wolff, H. Ekkehard. 2025. Secondary glottalisation in Central Chadic (Afroasiatic). Studies in African Linguistics 54.
sources.note: Nothing on Mbudum stress; cites only Mbudum zoŋgo 'donkey' (ex. 2b) for NAS+LAB prosody colouring.

sources.citation: Wolff, H. Ekkehard. 2025. Typology and evolution of minimal vowel systems in Central Chadic (Afroasiatic). Ch. 7 in Language Science Press volume 415.
sources.note: General Central Chadic remark only: epenthetic 'Schwa usually cannot undergo any lengthening or carry stress'; Mbudum not mentioned.

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The Phonology of Proto-Central Chadic. PhD Leiden, LOT 375. Utrecht: LOT.
sources.note: Nothing for Mbudum. Sec. 5.3.2 Daba group: Mbudum data from 'Ndokobaï in progress' (Mbudum Phonology; Lexique Mbudum); Mbudum has vowel PAL prosody, emergent LAB, *n > ŋ word-finally. Abstract: reconstruction is 'not including tone or stress'.

sources.citation: Ndokobai, Dadak. 2014. Esquisse phonologique de la langue mbudum. Yaoundé: CABTAL, février 2014. 22 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives item 76489; live sil.org Cloudflare-blocked, fetched sources via web.archive.org 20240617062050)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 (p.19): syllable is the tone-bearing unit; sec. 4 'Les tons' (p.21): two tones H/L, verb roots always L, nouns lexical tone, no tonal minimal pair found. The words accent/stress/accentuation never occur; 'prosodie' refers only to the palatalization prosody.

sources.citation: Lamberty, Melinda. 2003. A rapid appraisal survey of Mbedam (Mayo-Tsanaga Division, Far North Province). SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2003-013. 10 pp. (SIL archives item 8994; via web.archive.org)
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic survey only ('accent' p.9 is a questionnaire item about dialect differences).
